deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss is adjusting and calibrating a circle instrument with three axes (Reichenbach type). The first axis is the azimuthal one. The second axis tilts the circle. The third axis, perpendicular to the circle, carries the alhidade (index arm). B is the index reading belonging to a fixed setting of the drum (Trommel). The previous page used B in the task of bringing the third axis into one plane with the first and second.

(1) Text paragraph. B can be found independently of that task. Leave the azimuthal and drum screws untouched. Using only alhidade motion and rotation about the second axis, point the line of sight at one object twice and take the mean of the two index readings. For best results the two circle positions should differ as much as possible: one roughly vertical, one roughly horizontal. This requires the plane through the object and the second axis to be inclined about 45 degrees to the horizon. Then both a vertical and a horizontal circle position can contain the object.

(2) Observations of 5 Dec. The telescope had been removed and remounted, so the line of sight had to be redetermined. The target was the top of a pole, more precisely its intersection with a crescent-shaped attachment. Readings, with the adopted values:
- h (circle horizontal): 179°25'6", 25'2", 24'52", 24'52". Adopted: the settled last value, 179°24'52".
- v (circle vertical): 27'6", 27'35", 27'14", 27'29". Adopted: mean of the last two, 179°27'21.5".
- V (vertical, other face): 179°36'55", one reading.
- v': 25'59", 25'50", 25'44". Adopted: mean of the last two, 179°25'47".
- h': 26'24" (after a first 25'36"), 26'18", 26'18". Adopted: 179°26'18".
- A = 1°32'.

Reduction (formulas inferred by me from the numbers; all reproduce exactly). Write the four reversed readings as
- h = B + (p+a) - b
- v = B - (p+a) + b
- h' = B - (p+a) - b
- v' = B + (p+a) + b
- V = B + (p+a) - b + 2c

Each unknown is then obtained twice and averaged:
- B = (h+v)/2 = 179°26'6.75" and B = (h'+v')/2 = 179°26'2.50". Mean B = 179°26'4.625".
- p+a = (h-h')/2 = -43" and p+a = (v'-v)/2 = -47.25". Mean -45.125".
- b = (v'-h)/2 = +27.5" and b = (v-h')/2 = +31.75". Mean +29.625".
- c = (V - B + b - (p+a))/2 = (650.375 + 29.625 + 45.125)/2 = 362.5625" = 6'2.5625".
- Next line (letter struck out): B + A = 179°26'4.625" + 1°32' = 180°58'4.625".
- 'd =' is left blank.

(3) Last line. 'Beiläufig' p = 12.44". This is presumably the parallax-type term from the telescope's eccentricity at the known distance; on the next page p = 14.13" goes with distance about 2189 m. Then a = (p+a) - p = -45.125 - 12.44 = -57.565".

The whole page is a least-effort reversal (Umlegung) scheme. Each instrumental constant (index zero B, eccentricity plus axis error p+a, b, collimation c) is isolated from sums and differences of readings in reversed positions, each one twice.
errors: No arithmetic errors: all adopted values, means, and derived constants check exactly.

Choice of adopted raw values is not uniform and is not explained. For h and h' the last (settled) reading is taken. For v and v' the mean of the last two is taken. Early readings are discarded, presumably as settling drift.
V rests on a single reading, so c is less well determined than B, p+a and b, each of which is obtained twice.
'd =' is left without a value; the quantity on the struck-out line is just B + A.

results.what: Index zero B as the mean of index readings for the same object with the circle vertical and horizontal; the 45-degree arrangement maximizes the separation of the two positions.
results.modern_name: Instrument calibration by reversal (method of reversal / face-left face-right averaging)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of 18th-19th c. instrument makers and astronomers (Reichenbach, Bessel, etc.)

results.what: Separation of instrumental constants B, p+a, b, c from readings in four or five reversed positions, each determined twice, with p (eccentricity parallax) split off to get a.
results.modern_name: Error-separation by reversal measurements / instrument error budget (collimation, index error, eccentricity)
results.usually_credited_to: Routine geodetic-astronomical practice; systematic theory of instrumental errors often associated with Bessel

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine field notes on calibrating an instrument by reversal, with simple averaging of readings. They fit Gauss's well-documented Göttingen instrument work of the 1810s and contain no non-standard mathematics.

checkable.asserts: B=(h+v)/2 equals 179°26'6.75" (seconds counted from 179°; should be 0)

transcription_corrections: Second h' entry printed as '279.26.18' in the image is 179.26.18; the leading digit is an overwrite. The machine transcription already reads 179.
First h' value 179.25.36 stands apart above the column; it seems to be a superseded first reading.
'v = 179.27.6': the 7 is written over another digit, probably 4.
In 'v' = 179.25 47' the 5 is written over another digit; the adopted value is 179°25'47", the mean of 25'50" and 25'44".
The struck-out letter before '= 180.58.4.625' looks like a d/D overwritten. The value is B + A, not the blank 'd'.
'Alhidadenbewegung' (as in image), and 'die Spitze der Stange [auf] oder vielmehr ihr Schnitt' — 'auf' is struck through.
